title: Detector Selection and Experiment Design
scope: Detector feasibility, hardware audit, curated-dataset feasibility, evaluation protocol, game-specific metrics and integration design for a future trained detector.
non_goals: No changes to the perception architecture
No integration with the neural simulator, sensory scheduler, neural activity or plasticity

ram.note: Available memory fluctuates with other applications.

cpu_inference.marginal: 2.6-5M params, about 6-9 GFLOPs at 640 (YOLO11n, YOLOv8n, YOLOX-Tiny); measure latency

gpu_inference.counterfactual_estimate: With a CUDA stack, 0.9-5M params at 416-640 batch 1 would likely fit in 4 GB; a 20M-parameter RT-DETR inference might fit but is untested.

feasibility_consequences.workload: CPU inference, NanoDet or YOLOX-Nano at 416
feasibility_consequences.constraint: Latency unmeasured; RAM sufficient for inference.

feasibility_consequences.workload: CPU inference, YOLO11n or YOLOv8n at 640
feasibility_consequences.constraint: Must be measured; no real-time claim.
1.02 GiB available RAM is below a safe training budget.
No CUDA-enabled PyTorch or ONNX Runtime; installing one exceeds current free disk.

ranked_shortlist.rationale: Best size/accuracy/latency balance, Apache-2.0, native YOLO labels, 2.3 MB FP16. Training requires a separate environment or external hardware.
Apache-2.0, smallest training stack with no upper PyTorch pin; lower COCO accuracy and requires COCO JSON conversion.
Higher accuracy than YOLOX-Nano and still CPU-plausible, at about six times the compute and training cost.
Best tooling and highest accuracy in the shortlist, but AGPL-3.0 and a slower 640 input.
Mature but AGPL-3.0 and slower than YOLO11n.
Permissive but far too heavy for this CPU-only, 4 GB-laptop environment.

local_training_ranking.note: No upper PyTorch pin; smoke test required; Python 3.13 compatibility unverified.
Blocked by pinned torch<2.0 and pytorch-lightning<2.0; requires a separate Python 3.10 environment or relaxed pins.

temporal_data.note: subwayy1_1 contains two recordings with colliding frame IDs, so some f/f+1 filename pairs may cross recordings.

dataset.consequence: The first experiment is 14-class obstacle/train detection on group-held-out footage, not complete game perception.

data_rules: Resolve every image through the Phase 3B.1 manifest; never use the Roboflow folder split.
Never train or evaluate on the 12 quarantined images.
Keep raw images, labels, data.yaml and manifest read-only; write derived annotations outside the raw dataset.
Record hashes of manifest, data.yaml, derived annotations and weights.

protocol.primary_run: Train on fixed train groups, select and report on fixed valid groups.
protocol.variance: Train one model per LOGO fold and report mean +/- standard deviation across held-out groups.
protocol.test_split: None; no independent test split exists or can be formed from five recordings.
protocol.tuning: Hyperparameters and operating point selected on fixed valid only; not on LOGO validation.
protocol.partial_logo: If fewer than five folds are run, report exactly which folds and do not claim a five-fold variance estimate.

evaluation.pre_registered_selection_rule: Maximise macro recall over obstacle_low, obstacle_high and train at IoU 0.5, subject to micro precision >= 0.80. If unattainable, report best F1 and state that the constraint failed.
metrics: Precision, recall and F1 at IoU 0.5 (micro and macro) with support counts
AP@0.5 per class and mAP@0.5 over supported classes
Per-class AP with support counts; flag classes with fewer than 20 validation boxes
Confusion matrix at IoU 0.5 including background and false negatives
False-positive taxonomy: duplicate, localization, background, class confusion
False-negative taxonomy: no prediction, below threshold, localization, class mismatch
Precision-recall curves over a confidence sweep
Detector-only and full-pipeline latency (p50, p95, p99)
Peak process memory (RSS); VRAM only if a CUDA runtime is active

threshold_policy.nms: Class-wise, fixed IoU threshold (0.5 or 0.6) and fixed maximum detections, recorded per model.

latency_protocol.budget_caveat: Game frame rate is not verified; reference budgets are not game requirements.

reproducibility: Git commit, manifest hash, config hash, derived-label hash, weight hash
Package versions, hardware, thread count, exact commands and training duration
claims_not_allowed: The detector generalises beyond the measured groups
mAP proves lane understanding, distance estimation or temporal continuity
Detector accuracy demonstrates biological perception or neural coding
Validation performance is independent test performance

game_metrics.definition: Micro recall over GT boxes with configured game_state_role obstacle_low or obstacle_high.
Micro recall over boxtrain and train.
Assign GT and predicted boxes with the same LaneAssigner; report per lane.
game_metrics.caveat: Measures detection conditional on geometric lane, not true lane semantics.

game_metrics.definition: Fraction of matched detections whose assigned lane equals the GT box's assigned lane.
game_metrics.caveat: Same geometry on both sides; not independent lane truth.

game_metrics.definition: MAE and bias between predicted and GT bottom_edge_distance for matched boxes.
game_metrics.caveat: Measures box-bottom accuracy, not game or metric distance.

game_metrics.definition: Detection persistence, class-flip rate, lane-flip rate and box jitter across adjacent frames.
game_metrics.caveat: 833 candidate adjacent-frame pairs in valid is an upper bound: subwayy1_1 collides frame IDs across two recordings. No object-identity ground truth; requires new association code.

game_metrics.definition: FN rate for obstacle_low/obstacle_high boxes with distance proxy <= 0.4.
game_metrics.caveat: Dangerous is a design threshold, not a verified game rule; report sensitivity at 0.3/0.4/0.5.

game_metrics.definition: Agreement between predicted and GT-derived GameState (presence, type, lane, distance bucket, nearest-object selection).
game_metrics.caveat: GT-derived GameState is a deterministic label conversion, not true game state.
Outside the scope of this project phase.

integration.contract: Detector.detect(frame: ImageFrame) returns records in processed-image pixels; describe() returns JSON-safe metadata with test_only=false.
algorithm_steps: Read frame.pixels as RGB PIL and convert to NumPy.
Letterbox to model input, preserving aspect ratio and recording scale and padding.
Convert color order and normalization to match training exactly.
Run ONNX Runtime CPU (preferred) or PyTorch backend.
Decode boxes, scores and class IDs.
Apply class-wise NMS with a fixed IoU threshold.
Return RawDetection values with integer class IDs and float coordinates.
Do not clamp or drop malformed boxes; let DetectionValidator reject them.

preprocessing.color_order_risk: Perception supplies RGB; many OpenCV training pipelines use BGR. Choose one convention, record it and add a parity test.

class_ids.load_time_check: Class count, order and names must match ClassSchema; fail fast on mismatch; never remap.

confidence_nms.nms: class-wise, fixed IoU and max detections
confidence_nms.test_time_augmentation: not used in the first experiment

bbox_conversion.format: x1, y1, x2, y2 in model-input pixels
bbox_conversion.clipping: Do not clip to content; out-of-bounds boxes must be rejected by the validator.

device.cuda: Fail clearly if requested and unavailable; never silently fall back while reporting GPU use.

errors: No detections -> empty list, a legitimate result
integration.timing: perf_counter around detect; synchronize CUDA if used; model load time reported separately.
interface_additions_recommended_not_impl: Structured describe() metadata for weight hash, license, runtime, provider, input size and color order
scientific_boundary: Detector is a measurement instrument, not a model of the fly brain.
No import of brain_simulator, sensory scheduler or neural mapping.
No connection to neural activity or reward-modulated plasticity.
Fixed-connectome baseline and Phase 3A calibration remain untouched.

risks: No independent test split; all scores are group-held-out validation.
Training environment is memory- and disk-constrained; NanoDet's pinned PyTorch/Lightning versions conflict with Python 3.13 / torch 2.10.
GPU is present but unusable for ML without a CUDA stack that exceeds free disk.
Small objects: p10 heights of several obstacle classes are 15-27 px, becoming 6-11 px at 416 square.
Severe class imbalance: 1,617 train boxes versus 14 jump-electric and 24 boots-powerup train boxes.
Zero fixed-valid support for boots-powerup and jump-electric.
Class roles are name-derived hypotheses, not verified mechanics.
No player, coin, lane, distance, speed, jump or roll labels.
subwayy1_1 contains two recordings with colliding frame IDs and 296 duplicate-ID pairs; effective sample size is smaller than the image count.
Fixed validation uses recordings absent from training; scores are cross-recording, not random-sample estimates.
RGB/BGR, letterbox or normalization mismatch can silently reduce accuracy.
ONNX export drift can change decode/NMS behavior; parity testing is mandatory.
Ultralytics models are AGPL-3.0 and require a licensing decision.
mAP does not measure lane behavior, distance, temporal stability or latency.
Single-frame detections can flicker; temporal association is not implemented.
Vendor CPU latency numbers are not directly comparable to this machine.

model_artifact.onnx_export: same order as the weight file

notes: All values are planning estimates, not measurements.
A one-epoch or fixed-batch smoke test must replace them before a full run.
The 1.02 GiB available RAM at audit time is likely insufficient for training.

recommendation.summary: The detector choice and evaluation protocol are ready, but Phase 3B.2B.1 must not start until the environment, dependency and weight-download preconditions are resolved.
recommendation.preferred_model: NanoDet-Plus-m at 416x416, Apache-2.0, starting from COCO pretrained weights after license verification and download approval.
recommendation.fallback_if_local_training_required: YOLOX-Nano at 416x416, subject to a one-epoch smoke test; YOLOX-Tiny for higher accuracy.
recommendation.runtime: ONNX Runtime CPU, batch 1, explicit local weights, no auto-download.
recommendation.scope: 14-class v15 detection with obstacle/train emphasis; not complete game perception.
preconditions: Free at least about 4 GB of RAM and 5 GB of disk, or plan external training.
Choose a training environment: separate Python 3.10 for NanoDet, a smoke-tested YOLOX path, or external GPU training with ONNX weights brought back.
Approve every new package and version before installation; do not upgrade existing PyTorch, NumPy, Pillow or ONNX Runtime without a separate decision.
Verify checkpoint license and source, record SHA-256, and download only with approval; do not commit weights.
Approve the derived-annotation directory and keep raw dataset, data.yaml and manifest read-only.
Freeze the fixed-split/LOGO protocol and the pre-registered operating-point rule before inspecting results.
Pass a one-epoch or fixed-batch smoke test with measured time, peak RSS and disk use before full training.
recommendation.stop_condition: If the preconditions cannot be met, stop before training and retain the design. Do not reduce the scientific protocol silently to fit the machine.
must_not_happen: Train on the Roboflow folder split
Report COCO mAP as v15 accuracy
Infer unlabelled player, coin, lane, speed or distance ground truth
Connect the detector to the simulator, scheduler or plasticity code
Claim biological perception from detection accuracy
